title: runtime/guards.json — pre-dispatch intent guards (ADR-005 Part 2)
description: Deterministic corrections applied to a classified intent BEFORE the action dispatcher sees it. These are not tuning knobs: without them a help-phrased utterance fires the command it asks about. Distinct from runtime/routing.json, which decides what to do when confidence is LOW; a guard fires regardless of confidence. Additive section — a runtime that does not find this file loses the corrections but still loads the pack.

help_marker.description: Redirects a command intent to its help counterpart when the utterance is phrased as a question. 'how do i turn up the volume' must show help, not change the volume.

markers.description: Portable-subset regex (spec/bundle/portable-regex.md, compiler stage 10) matched against the normalized utterance. A match arms the redirect.

pairs.description: classified intent id -> help intent id to substitute. Both sides must exist in the pack's intent set (compiler-enforced).

polarity.description: Contradiction guards: utterances whose surface intent is negated by a polarity cue ('don't turn it up'). Empty until authored; the section exists so a runtime can bind it without a format change.

redirect.description: Intent to substitute. Omitted means suppress to the out-of-scope fallback.

bare_value.description: Suppresses an intent when the WHOLE utterance is nothing but one of a closed entity's values. A memory is named 'Outdoors'; a user who says only 'outdoors' has not asked for anything, and a device that switches programs on a stray word heard by an always-on mic is the worst failure this pack can produce. Switching stays available through the explicit forms ('switch to outdoors') and through the slot prompt, neither of which this guard touches.

intent.description: Intent id to suppress. Must exist in the pack (compiler-enforced).

entity.description: Closed entity whose values arm the guard. Must exist in the pack (compiler-enforced). The values are NOT copied here — the entity remains the single source, so a new value is covered with no change to this file.

redirect.description: Intent to substitute. Omitted means suppress to the out-of-scope fallback.

slot_passthrough.description: Entities whose VALUES the pack cannot own. A user names their own custom memory, so that name can never appear in a build-time enum; without this a runtime asks for the name, fails to match what it is told, and re-asks until the slot budget is spent. An entry says: for this entity, when enum matching fails, the spoken name may be handed to the host instead — marked unresolved, never as a recognised value. `carrier` is what makes it narrow: on the FIRST turn the utterance must carry an explicit change verb, because an always-open microphone must not read 'put it on the shelf' as a request for a memory called 'the shelf'. Additive; a runtime that ignores this section keeps today's re-prompt behaviour.

entity.description: The entity whose values the pack cannot enumerate.

carrier.description: Portable-subset pattern, anchored at the start, matching the explicit request wrapper. What remains after it is the candidate name. Only consulted on an unprompted first turn.

trailing.description: Optional portable-subset pattern for a domain noun to strip off the end ("switch to temp memory" -> "temp").
